newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Schroders warns of HK banks' exposure to property.
newsitem.headline: Schroders warns of HK banks' exposure to property.

text.p: Hong Kong banks' increased exposure to the rising property market could affect the soundness of the territory's financial system in the long term, Schroder Investment Management (Hong Kong) Ltd said on Tuesday.

"Now the mortgage lending is steady and the default rate is low. The economy is also steady. But if property prices continue to rise, that will affect the soundness (of the financial sector)," Schroder director David Lui told a news conference.
Prices of residential properties have surged in recent months, driven as least in part by speculation. There is the high prices could mean more chance of default on the mortgage loans.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the de facto central bank, said in late May additional restraints in mortgage lending policies might be required as growth in lending had resulted in an increase in banks' property exposure.
Gross new loans made during April rose by 35.2 percent to a record high of HK$22.7 billioin compared with a drop of 10.6 percent in March.
In January, the HKMA already recommended the maximum loan to value ratio for more expensive properties should be reduced.
Lui said the HKMA's steps were appropriate to ensure the exposure of banks to the sector did not undermine the long term soundness of the financial system.

A Schroders report released on Tuesday said supply of private residential units in the territory in the next few years was expected to be too low to meet demands in view of an anticipated strong population growth. It gave no figures.
Lui forecast earnings of Hong Kong-listed banks to grow an average 15 percent this year, lower than the 20 percent growth rate of last year.
He said that was due to a narrowed interest spread which resulted partly from price competition for mortgage loans.
